core_obligations: Prove the base case (proof lines 2656-2675): for p = 0 the statement follows from the corresponding result in the chapter Sites, and the author checks that its hypotheses are satisfied, using (1) and (2) with the fibred square to get a surjection from an element of S onto any sheaf, and using (3) together with (5) to see that products of elements of S are quasi-compact.

Set up the induction (proof lines 2678-2686): assume the result for all degrees at most p_0 and for all topoi admitting a set S with (1)-(5); arguing as in the same-chapter companion lemma, it suffices to show that H^{p_0+1}(C, I) = 0 for a filtered colimit I = colim I_lambda of injective abelian sheaves.

Use the spectral sequence (proof lines 2687-2725): choose K -> * surjective with K in S and use the spectral sequence E_1^{p,q} = H^q(K^{p+1}, I) converging to H^{p+q}(C, I); rewriting H^q(K^{p+1}, I) as H^q(C/K^{p+1}, j^{-1}I) and using that j^{-1} commutes with filtered colimits, the induction hypothesis identifies the E_1 terms with the colimit of the corresponding terms for I_lambda, which vanish in the relevant range by injectivity.

Check that the induction hypothesis applies (proof lines 2728-2785): one has to verify that the localized topos C/K^{p+1} admits a set of objects satisfying conditions (1)-(5); the author carries this check out, which is what allows the induction to run inside the localized topoi.
proof_roadmap: Base case p = 0: invoke the corresponding statement about filtered colimits of global sections, verifying its hypotheses with (1)-(3) and quasi-compactness.
Induction: reduce to the vanishing of H^{p0+1} on a filtered colimit of injectives.
Compute with the Cech-to-cohomology spectral sequence of a surjection K -> * with K in S, using that restriction to C/K commutes with filtered colimits.
Verify that the localized topoi satisfy the same hypotheses so that the induction hypothesis applies, and conclude.
difficulty_reason: The lemma establishes the commutation of cohomology with filtered colimits for a site carrying a set S of sheaves satisfying five conditions, including quasi-compactness of its members (statement lines 2629-2653). The proof is an induction on the cohomological degree with two substantial parts. The base case is reduced to the corresponding statement on colimits of global sections, whose hypotheses are checked through (1)-(3) and quasi-compactness (proof lines 2656-2675). The induction step reduces the assertion to the vanishing of H^{p0+1} on a filtered colimit of injective sheaves and computes with the Cech-to-cohomology spectral sequence E_1^{p,q} = H^q(K^{p+1}, I) = H^q(C/K^{p+1}, j^{-1}I), where commutation of j^{-1} with filtered colimits and the induction hypothesis in the localized topoi give the vanishing (proof lines 2687-2725). The delicate part, which the author writes out separately, is the check that the localized topoi themselves admit a set satisfying (1)-(5), without which the induction could not be applied (proof lines 2728-2785). The claim is H2: a long but fully written-out induction.
